The existing county road system had been upgraded somewhat prior to mining activities, including paving of a portion of the county road reaching the mine site from Hardin. Under the present mining operation, construction of haul roads has been limited to the mining area itself.
Waste Disposal
Waste water from the plant site is wholly contained in an evaporation lagoon. This lagoon would be buried at the end of mining operations on the lease. Combustible materials are destroyed in a burn pit.

Noncombustibles are buried in the mine.
POTENTIAL DEVELOPMENT
Analysis Guidelines
Future development of coal resources on Tract II and III will depend upon many factors which are not known at present. The minimum production stipulations in the amended leases call for mining of 10 million tons of coal annually from Tract III by 1981, and 15 million tons by 1989. For Tract II, annual coal production would reach 4 million tons by 1982 and would presumably remain constant until the reserves of 350 million tons are depleted in the year 2070. Westmoreland Resources has repeatedly stated that their present plans call for coal development at the rates as specified in the amended leases. However, it must be recognized that other patterns of development may occur due to changes in economic, technological and other factors.
